ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC$, and the bisectors of $\angle BAC$ and $\angle ACB$ intersect at point $D$. Given that $\angle ADC=130^\circ$, find the measure of $\angle BAC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $AB=AC$, and $AE$ bisects $\angle BAC$,\\
it follows that $AE\perp BC$ (for an isosceles triangle, three lines coincide),\\
since $\angle ADC=130^\circ$,\\
it follows $\angle CDE=50^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle DCE=90^\circ-\angle CDE=40^\circ$, and since $CD$ bisects $\angle ACB$,\\
it follows $\angle ACB=2\angle DCE=80^\circ$.\\
Since $AB=AC$,\\
it follows $\angle B=\angle ACB=80^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle BAC=180^\circ-(\angle B+\angle ACB)=\boxed{20^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is at the top, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and BC is the base; from A to the base, a line segment is drawn to E, point D is on this line segment, and line segment CD is drawn from C to D. Therefore, the figure shows D inside the triangle, and AD and CD respectively correspond to the angle bisectors mentioned in the problem. Then reason: The problem gives AB=AC, so triangle ABC is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles satisfy ∠B=∠C. Also because the angle bisectors of ∠BAC and ∠ACB intersect at D, D is the incenter. Use the formula for incenter D: ∠ADC = 90° + 1/2∠B. It is known that ∠ADC=130°, so 130° = 90° + 1/2∠B, giving 1/2∠B=40°, that is, ∠B=80°. Since AB=AC, ∠C=∠B=80°. Therefore ∠BAC = 180° - 80° - 80° = 20°.
